article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 75% Indica / 25% Sativa
Genetics: Blueberry × Mazar-i-Sharif
Breeder: Plantamaster Seeds
THC Content: 20–25%
CBD Content: Around 1% or lower
Terpene Profile: pinene , myrcene , and limonene
Primary Flavors: Berry, tart fruit, herbs, earth, spice, hash
Flowering Time (Indoor): 56–63 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late September to mid-October
Indoor Yield: 500–600 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: Medium to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Supernova brings together two very different branches of old-school cannabis breeding and turns them into a potent, resin-heavy marijuana cultivar with considerably more character than its space-age name alone suggests. Plantamaster Seeds developed the strain from Blueberry and Mazar-i-Sharif genetics, pairing the fruit, color, and aromatic complexity of the Blueberry family with the dense flower structure and deeply relaxing character associated with Afghan cannabis . The resulting plant leans strongly indica, but its high does not always behave like a purely sedating weed strain . Mental clarity and euphoria can arrive before the heavier physical sensations take hold, giving the experience a distinct progression rather than an immediate descent into couch-lock.

Finished flowers can be exceptionally resinous, with bright to deeper green calyxes, abundant orange pistils, and a thick coating of trichomes. Blue or violet coloration may appear in some plants, particularly when cooler conditions activate the pigmentation inherited from Blueberry. Aroma moves between berries, tart fruit, herbs, earth, and hash-like spice, providing a profile that feels more traditional than the candy-heavy flavor combinations common in many newer hybrids. With THC levels capable of approaching 25%, Supernova occupies the stronger end of the cannabis spectrum and is generally more appropriate for experienced consumers than for someone still learning their tolerance.
Genetics and Lineage

Plantamaster Seeds created Supernova by crossing Blueberry with Mazar-i-Sharif, producing an indica-dominant hybrid commonly described as approximately 75% indica. The Blueberry side contributes much more than its name implies. Descended from DJ Short ‘s celebrated breeding work, Blueberry genetics are valued for sweet berry aromas, colorful flower expression, resin production, and a relaxing yet often mentally pleasant effect. Those traits are easy to recognize in well-grown Supernova, particularly when ripe berry aromas emerge alongside violet pigmentation.

Mazar-i-Sharif adds the Afghan foundation. Cannabis originating around Mazar-i-Sharif in northern Afghanistan has long been associated with broad-leaf plant structure, copious resin, hash production , and a physically substantial effect. Bringing that genetic influence into the cross gives the cultivar a sturdier, more traditional indica character. Dense flower formation, earthy undertones, hash-like spice, and a tendency toward deeper late-stage relaxation all fit naturally within that heritage.

What makes the pairing particularly effective is the contrast between the parents. Blueberry brings brighter fruit and aromatic softness, while the Afghan side supplies weight, resin, and depth. Neither side completely overwhelms the other. Instead, mature buds can move from tart berry and sweet fruit at first inspection toward musk, herbs, earth, and old-school hash as the flowers are broken apart.
Effects and Experience

Supernova often announces itself mentally before its indica genetics become obvious physically. Early in the experience, mood may rise noticeably while thoughts take on a more absorbed or focused quality. Music, conversation, movies, gaming, and other relaxed activities can become more immersive, and a gentle creative streak may emerge. The cerebral component gives the first portion of the high more movement than consumers might expect from a heavily indica-leaning cultivar.

Physical effects gather gradually. What begins as a comfortable loosening through the shoulders and limbs can develop into much deeper relaxation as the THC reaches its peak. Remaining active is possible at a conservative dose, but larger amounts can make sitting down considerably more attractive. Hunger is another commonly associated effect, making food particularly appealing once the high has settled in. Reports surrounding the cultivar frequently describe a combination of happiness, relaxation, euphoria, and eventual sleepiness.

Potency changes the equation considerably. At THC levels approaching 25%, a large inhalation or an unnecessarily fast second dose can move the experience from calm to disorienting. Dry mouth, dry eyes, temporary short-term memory impairment, dizziness, or anxious thoughts are possible with THC-rich marijuana, particularly among inexperienced or sensitive consumers. A modest starting amount leaves more room to appreciate the strain’s transition from mental uplift into body relaxation.
Medical Benefits

The combination of substantial THC and a relaxing late-stage effect makes Supernova potentially interesting to medical marijuana consumers dealing with chronic discomfort or conditions that interfere with rest. Its initial euphoric quality may provide a temporary psychological break from persistent symptoms, while the heavier physical portion of the experience can make inactivity and relaxation easier. Appetite stimulation may also be useful to some patients experiencing reduced interest in food, although responses to high-THC cannabis differ substantially between individuals.

Clinical research supports a cautious interpretation of these potential benefits. A 2021 systematic review and meta-analysis of 32 randomized clinical trials involving 5,174 adults found that medical cannabis and cannabinoids produced small improvements in chronic pain and sleep quality compared with placebo, while also increasing temporary adverse effects including dizziness, drowsiness, nausea, and impaired attention. The trials evaluated cannabis-based treatments rather than Supernova specifically, so the findings provide context for THC-rich marijuana rather than proof that one particular strain treats pain.

Sleep is another reason some consumers may choose an indica-dominant cultivar later in the evening. A separate systematic review concluded that medical cannabis and cannabinoids may improve impaired sleep among people with chronic pain, although the overall benefit was small. Supernova should therefore be viewed as a potent cannabis option whose effects may overlap with symptoms some patients are trying to manage—not as a proven treatment for insomnia, anxiety, depression, PTSD, or any other specific medical disorder.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Berry notes provide the most recognizable entry point, but the profile becomes considerably earthier once the flower is handled. An intact bud may smell of tart blueberries or mixed dark fruit. Grinding it exposes herbal, spicy, musky, and hash-like components underneath, producing a combination that bridges fruity cannabis breeding with the heavier aromas of traditional Afghan weed.

On the inhale, fruit can seem sweeter than the aroma initially suggests. Berry and mild sugary flavors appear first before giving way to dry herbs, earth, peppery spice, and a lingering hash character. Proper curing matters considerably with this cultivar. Over-dried flower can flatten the fruit and emphasize harsh herbal notes, while carefully stored buds retain much more of the contrast between Blueberry sweetness and the darker Afghan foundation.

Pinene, myrcene, and limonene have been reported among the prominent terpenes in commercial Supernova flower, with pinene appearing as the most abundant terpene in some samples. Those rankings should not be treated as permanent genetic specifications. Terpene concentration varies with phenotype, growing environment, harvest maturity, curing conditions, and storage, so laboratory testing of the individual batch remains the best guide to its actual terpene composition.
Growing Information

Supernova is a photoperiod marijuana plant with a moderate growth profile and an indoor flowering period of roughly 56 to 63 days. Archived breeder information places flowering at approximately 60 days and indoor production around 500–600 grams per square meter under suitable conditions. Plants tend to form strong central flowers while maintaining useful lateral branching, making the cultivar adaptable to several indoor training methods.

The canopy benefits from thoughtful pruning rather than aggressive intervention. Removing weak lower growth allows more energy to reach productive flowering sites, while moderate low-stress training can help expose secondary branches to stronger light. As buds gain density, airflow becomes increasingly important. Maintaining reasonable humidity through late bloom helps protect tightly packed flowers from mold and also gives the heavy trichome layer a better opportunity to mature cleanly.

Outdoors, the plant is best matched with locations that provide a sufficiently long, sunny growing season without excessive autumn moisture. Harvest can arrive from late September into October depending on latitude and phenotype. Cooler nights may encourage blue or violet pigmentation inherited from the Blueberry parent, though color should never be used as the primary indicator of maturity. Trichome development, flower swelling, pistil progression, and the plant’s overall ripeness provide much more useful information when choosing the final harvest window.
FAQ
Is Supernova an indica or sativa?

Supernova is an indica-dominant hybrid commonly described as approximately 75% indica. Its physical relaxation reflects that genetic bias, although the early portion of the high can feel more cerebral, euphoric, and mentally engaging than a traditional heavy indica.
What are the genetics of Supernova?

Plantamaster Seeds bred Supernova from Blueberry × Mazar-i-Sharif. Blueberry supplies fruit, color, and aromatic sweetness, while Mazar-i-Sharif contributes Afghan resin production, dense flower structure, earthiness, and a stronger body-oriented character.
How much THC does Supernova have?

THC levels are commonly placed around 20–25%, with breeder-associated records listing approximately 25%. Actual potency depends on phenotype, cultivation, harvest timing, and the individual batch, so laboratory results should take precedence over a generic strain percentage.
What does Supernova weed taste like?

The flavor combines tart berry and sweet fruit with herbs, earth, spice, and a hash-like finish. Blueberry genetics provide much of the fruit character, while the Afghan side adds a darker, more resinous flavor beneath it.
How long does Supernova take to flower?

Indoor flowering generally lasts about 56–63 days, or roughly eight to nine weeks. Outdoor plants can mature from late September into October depending on climate and latitude. Indoor yields of approximately 500–600 g/m² have been associated with the cultivar under productive growing conditions.
Final Thoughts on Supernova

Supernova represents a style of cannabis breeding built around recognizable legacy genetics rather than an elaborate collection of modern dessert cultivars. Blueberry gives the strain its fruit, occasional purple coloration, and softer aromatic side, while Mazar-i-Sharif anchors the cross with Afghan resin, earthiness, dense flowers, and physical weight. That balance produces weed with enough flavor to interest terpene-focused consumers while retaining the substantial body effect many people expect from an indica-dominant hybrid.

Its strongest quality may be the way the experience changes over time. An initially euphoric and mentally engaging high gradually becomes calmer, heavier, and more physical, allowing the same flower to occupy different territory depending on dose and timing. Add a THC ceiling around 25%, an approximately eight-to-nine-week flowering period, strong trichome production, and potential indoor yields around 500–600 g/m², and Supernova offers meaningful appeal on both sides of the garden. For cannabis enthusiasts who appreciate berry flavors but want something earthier and more traditionally Afghan underneath, this cultivar provides a distinctive combination of fruit, resin, potency, and deep relaxation.
